description_full: Japan Exchange Group, Inc. operates as a financial instruments exchange holding company in Japan. The company engages in the operation of financial instruments exchange markets for trading listed securities and derivatives instruments to market users; publication of stock prices and quotations; provides market facilities for trading of commodity derivatives, physical commodities, and commodity index futures; self-regulatory operations, such as listing examination, listed company compliance, market surveillance, and inspections and examinations of trading participants. The company also provides clearing and settlement, and market-related services for transactions through proprietary trading systems (PTS), over-the-counter derivative transactions, and over-the-counter government bond transactions. The company was incorporated in 1949 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: Japan Exchange Group, Inc. is a large-cap financial services business with a $13.7B market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 42% against a 8% cost of capital — a 34-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 54% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $627M in free cash flow — roughly 60 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.76× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
